newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil down on high stocks.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil down on high stocks.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps extended its early day losses late afternoon on Thursday amid high stocks prompting one refiner to ship cargoes out for storage outside its refinery complex, traders said.
"The market is suffering from this prompt overhang and the contango is widening because of this," one trader said.
July paper was last quoted at $23.15/$23.30 down about 10 cents from this morning and from Wednesday's $23.45/$23.55, brokers said.
The market traded earlier in the day $23.27, $23.25, 23.22 and $23.20, they said.
Traders said lower prices were mainly due to the lack of prompt buying interest in Singapore which led to a freefall of prices early this week.

The high stock level was refleced in data released by the Singapore's Trade Development Board showed that middle distillate stocks have risen by 993,000 barrels to 11.236 million barrels for the week ending June 11.
The stocks are at their highest since at least Janaury 1994.
The situation was made worse by the inability of Singapore refiners to find outlets for their product due to the abundant arbitrage cargoes still unsold in Singapore.
As a result, the refiners have started to sell their forward cargoes at discount to prevailing spot prices with some cargoes sold at about 10 cents below spot prices.
The weak prompt market has also widened the swaps time spread with the July/August spread valued at minus 20 cents from an earlier minus 10 cents, brokers said.
Physical gas oil on Wednesday rebounded slightly to above $23.00 per barrel after trading at $22.90 on Tuesday, with no deals concluded.
Fuel oil swaps were steady despite the fall in crude with July was indicated at $98.50/$99.50.
